sense: a group of words, an expression

terms.comment: Properly a speaking, and in Cicero a way of speaking: ēmendāta et Latīna locūtiō (Brut. 258). The sense “phrase, expression” is post-Augustan (Gellius); in Quintilian 1.5.2 it is even a single word (Lewis & Short).
The everyday way: hīs verbīs, in these words; ad verbum, word for word (Cic. Fin. 1.4).
A fixed form, chiefly of law and ritual (testāmentōrum fōrmulae, Cic.), so a set phrase; also a rule or method (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a way of putting it, an expression
terms.comment: Classically a speaking or pleading, a style of delivery; “the use of a word or phrase” in Quintilian and Gellius, and a single word in the grammarians (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: multam nōs quoque apud veterēs scrīptōrēs locūtiōnum tālium cōpiam offendimus
phrases.english: we too have come upon a great many phrases of that kind in the old writers

sources: Lewis & Short: locutio · Lewis & Short: verbum · Lewis & Short: formula · Lewis & Short: dictio
